To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pulmonary phagocytic response to the separate and combined impacts (at the doses tested) of MnO2 and CrO4 particles is characterized by the following features.

the combined impact of MnO2 and CrO4 particulates is additive with respect to the cytotoxicity for peritoneal macrophae in vitro and the pulmonary phagocytic response in vivo, but the former is not related to the latter.

the combined impact of MnO2 and CrO4 particles on the rat pulmonary phagocytic response is synergistic and that the NL recruitment is an efficient auxiliary mechanism of the pulmonary particle elimination.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combined toxicity of MnO2 and CrO4 particles is not additive, but synergistic, and that the synergism is of the type "synergism of the first order" for both cytotoxic and cytostimulative effects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cytotoxicity and pulmonary phagocytic response of microscale Mn2O4 and BaCrO2 particles are additive in nature and that the type of the combined toxicity of both particles depends on the particular effect this type of toxicity is assessed for and its dose-dependent level.
the combined impact of MnO2 and Cr(VI) particulates in lungs was not more toxic than the separate impact of the same particles.

the combined impacts of both particulates were not simply additive but synergistic in terms of the cytotoxicity for the rat peritoneal AMs and antagonistic in terms of their ability to induce the phagocytotic NL recruitment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phagocytosed particles may cause the damage of AMs, and the latter may be compensated for by the NL recruitment.
the phagocytotic response to combined impacts of low-solvability metal-containing particles is a very complex phenomenon.
the combined impact of MnO2 and CrO4 particles on rat lungs is not additive but rather synergistic.
